newsitem.title: USA: PacifiCorp to acquire TPC for about $288 million.
newsitem.headline: PacifiCorp to acquire TPC for about $288 million.

text.p: PacifiCorp said Wednesday it agreed to acquire TPC Corp., a natural gas marketing company based in Houston, for $288 million.
PacifiCorp, an Oregon-based electricity wholesaler, said that on Tuesday, March 18, it will begin a tender offer to purchase all outstanding TPC shares for $13.41 per share.
TPC stock rose $2 to $13.125 on the New York Stock Exchange. PacifiCorp was unchanged at $20.625, also on the NYSE.
PacifiCorp said it expected the acquisition of TPC will be slightly dilutive to its earnings in 1997 and add slightly to earnings afterward.

TPC is involved in gas gathering systems in and near the Gulf of Mexico and in salt dome storage projects at the Moss Bluff market hub in Texas and the Egan market hub in Louisiana. Its other core business is natural gas marketing to utilities in the Midwest and Northeast.
"This transaction is key in establishing PacifiCorp as a full service energy company," said Fred Buckman, PacifiCorp president and chief executive officer.
"The TPC assets and skills compliment our extensive electric and coal assets and skills which we believe give us a competitive advantage in energy markets," he said.

PacifiCorp is the highest volume investor-owned wholesaler of electric energy west of the Mississippi River. Based in Portland, Oregon, it serves 1.4 million retail customers in the west and 550,000 retail customers in Australia.
